Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)  
- 19-year-old female with under one week of dysuria, urinary frequency, aching suprapubic pain, and recent pink discoloration of urine consistent with hematuria  
- No systemic features such as fever, flank pain, nausea, vomiting, or abnormal vaginal discharge  
- Past history of IBS with no new bowel symptoms  
- Allergy to clindamycin noted  
- Differential diagnosis consistent with an uncomplicated urinary tract infection (cystitis) – high likelihood given classic symptoms and hematuria  
- Medium likelihood of sexually transmitted infection (urethritis), given sexual history and symptoms, but absence of unusual discharge lowers probability  
- Low likelihood considerations include urinary tract stone (no flank pain or colicky features), interstitial cystitis (acute onset makes this unlikely), and bladder or urethral neoplasm (very unlikely given age and acute presentation)  
- No evidence or history of trauma, congenital abnormalities, or diabetes-related urinary symptoms  
- Conflict noted: DDx includes STI and neoplasm as possible causes; transcript supports UTI as primary diagnosis, STI possibility acknowledged but no signs or discharge reported  

Management Plan  
- Start antibiotic treatment with either Trimethoprim or Nitrofurantoin (3-day course) – dose/route/frequency not documented  
- Collect and analyze urine sample to confirm diagnosis and guide antibiotic choice  
- Advise increased fluid intake for adequate hydration  
- Use simple analgesia such as paracetamol if pain develops  
- Educate on symptoms requiring urgent review: fever, flank/back pain, vomiting  
- Follow-up if symptoms persist or worsen after one week  
- Provide advice on substance use; discourage regular marijuana use  
- No immediate referral indicated, pending urine results

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):  
- Urinary tract infection (cystitis) – High likelihood: Classic symptoms of dysuria, frequency, suprapubic pain, hematuria; no systemic features; supported by clinical presentation in transcript  
- Sexually transmitted infection (urethritis/cervicitis) – Moderate likelihood: Unprotected sex and dysuria present; no discharge or other signs reported, lowers probability but cannot be excluded definitively  
- Urinary tract stone – Low likelihood: Hematuria and pain present but absence of flank pain and colicky character argue against  
- Interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome – Low likelihood: Typically chronic and no hematuria, inconsistent with acute presentation  
- Bladder or urethral neoplasm – Low likelihood: Very rare at this age with acute symptoms
